jamal (customer-sre): Hey team, customer reports intermittent NXDOMAIN for api.svc.internal from some hosts in their VPC after we onboarded Redwood Private. Works from their bastion but fails from app nodes. They see spikes of 502s on our side.
priya (support): Can you paste a failing dig and a working dig from the bastion? Also which AWS account/VPCs are involved?
jamal (customer-sre): Sure. VPCs: cust-prod (10.10.0.0/16), redwood-private (10.20.0.0/16) peered. From failing app host (10.10.5.23):
```
$ dig @169.254.169.253 api.svc.internal +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3-1ubuntu1.13-Ubuntu <<>> @169.254.169.253 api.svc.internal +short
; (1 server found)
;; global options: +cmd
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
(we use the VPC resolver IP 169.254.169.253 per AWS)
From bastion (10.10.1.12):
```
$ dig api.svc.internal +short
10.20.2.10
```
jamal (customer-sre): So bastion resolves fine, apps get NXDOMAIN/timeouts.
alex (infra): Interesting. That suggests different resolver path. Bastion might be using a different resolver config (maybe /etc/resolv.conf pointing to VPC resolver but caching). Are there any Route53 Resolver rules or conditional forwarding in place?
maria (eng-platform): I pulled the account config: cust-prod has a Route53 private hosted zone "svc.internal" associated only to cust-prod VPC. Redwood-private also provisioned a private hosted zone with the same name in the redwood account and associated to redwood-private VPC. They set up a Route53 Resolver outbound rule in cust-prod to forward queries for svc.internal to the redwood resolver IP (52.23.11.5) which we expect. The rule target IP list references 52.23.11.5.
priya (support): Does 52.23.11.5 still accept DNS? Any firewall/egress allowlist issues?
jamal (customer-sre): I tried to curl 52.23.11.5:53 from app host and it timed out (ICMP blocked, but TCP 53 also no response). From bastion it connects.
alex (infra): Two suspicions: (1) the app subnets are in a private AZ route with different NAT / egress that blocks outbound to our resolver, (2) the resolver IP in the customer's target list is stale or our resolver SG changed. Can someone run a dig to the resolver from both hosts?
maria (eng-platform): I ran tcpdump on 52.23.11.5 side (internal infra) and see SYNs/UDP queries from bastion IPs but nothing from app host IPs. That implies app traffic isn't reaching our edge. Could be NACL / SG / VPC route.
priya (support): Customer says they have an egress allowlist for external DNS endpoints (security policy). They added 52.23.11.5 earlier but that was for TCP/UDP 53. Have they got NAT gateways per subnet?
jamal (customer-sre): Confirmed: app subnets route egress via NAT gateway nat-0a1b2c, bastion egress is direct IGW. NAT gateway uses a different Elastic IP (EIP) than we expect. Their egress allowlist only allows EIP 198.51.100.17 (bastion) — not the NAT EIP 203.0.113.9. So outbound from apps to 52.23.11.5 is getting dropped upstream at the customer's perimeter appliance.
alex (infra): That explains asymmetric behavior. Bastion works because its EIP is allowlisted. Apps are NATed to a different EIP that's not allowlisted, so packets get dropped before reaching our resolver — causing timeouts -> DNS client treats as SERVFAIL/NXDOMAIN. Two remediation paths: (A) have customer add NAT EIP 203.0.113.9 to their egress allowlist for 52.23.11.5:53 (UDP/TCP), or (B) configure the customer's resolver rule to forward to our resolver via a peered/private path (if available) or use cross-account VPC association instead of forwarding.
maria (eng-platform): Also noticed the customer's resolver rule had two target IPs; one is 52.23.11.5 (current) and another 52.23.11.6 (decom'd last week). If NAT EIP were allowlisted only for 52.23.11.6 earlier, things could flip as we rotated. Recommend customer to allow both current resolver IPs or use our documented dedicated resolver endpoint they get in onboarding.
priya (support): Action items: jamal — ask them to temporarily allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to 52.23.11.5 and 52.23.11.6 from the NAT EIP 203.0.113.9 and retest. alex/maria — we'll prepare a short runbook explaining: VPC association vs resolver forwarding, how NAT EIPs affect DNS egress allowlists, and how to validate with dig/tcpdump.
jamal (customer-sre): Will do. Meanwhile, quick repro steps for support note:
1) From failing app host: `dig @169.254.169.253 api.svc.internal +tries=1 +time=2` => times out/SERVFAIL.
2) From bastion: `dig api.svc.internal +short` => returns 10.20.2.10.
3) From app host, `curl -s -v telnet://52.23.11.5:53` => times out (shows NAT EIP 203.0.113.9 in packet capture).
4) On our side, `tcpdump -n src 203.0.113.9 and port 53` => no hits.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident record created: INC-2026-2345 (private-dns-forwarding-blocked) assigned to infra oncall.
alex (infra): If customer can't change allowlist quickly, we can provide a temporary workaround: create a private hosted zone in their account and associate it to the app VPCs (if they prefer not to forward). But that's a config change on their side.
maria (eng-platform): I'll draft the runbook now and include commands to validate resolver targets and EIP paths. Also include how to check Route53 "VPC Association" vs "Resolver Rule" in console + awscli snippets.
priya (support): Thanks. jamal, once customer adds the NAT EIP to allowlist and confirms, we'll re-run a small canary to ensure no more NXDOMAIN. Please paste results here. :thumbsup:
jamal (customer-sre): Customer added EIP to allowlist and I can now dig from app host: `dig @169.254.169.253 api.svc.internal +short` -> `10.20.2.10`. Confirmed. They also removed the stale 52.23.11.6 target.
priya (support): Closing loop: root cause = egress allowlist on customer's perimeter only allowed bastion EIP; app NAT EIP wasn't allowlisted so forwarded queries to our resolver never arrived. Secondary contributing factor: stale target IP in resolver rule during rotation. Documented fix + runbook in the internal KB. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: INC-2026-2345 status -> resolved
